PullRequest.Title: editor: avoid duplicate border on maximized editor groups
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Fixes #339772.

Split-view separators were drawn before every non-first DOM child, including the first visible view after maximizing an editor group. This left an extra separator next to the editor card's outer border.

Draw separators only between visible views. Regression tests cover both orientations, hidden leading and middle views, maximizing the last view, and restoring visibility.

### Verification

- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\base\test\browser\ui\splitview\splitview.test.ts --run src\vs\base\test\browser\ui\grid\gridview.test.ts --reporter dot` — 64 passed. The two new cases fail against the original CSS.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `pnpm run eslint src\vs\base\test\browser\ui\splitview\splitview.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm run stylelint src\vs\base\browser\ui\splitview\splitview.css` — passed.
- `pnpm run compile-client` — blocked by missing Microsoft authentication extension dependencies in the local setup. The client-only build, client type-check, and targeted tests above passed on the rebased candidate.
- Manually reproduced and verified in Code OSS on Windows with Modern UI and the 2026 dark theme. Maximizing either group leaves one outer border; restoring both groups retains their separator. Before/after captures were reviewed locally.

To test: open two editor groups side by side, activate the right group, and run **View: Toggle Maximize Editor Group**. Check the left edge, then restore and repeat with the left group.

Light/high-contrast themes and the full workbench test suite were not exercised.

Scenarios.Scenario: Maximize or restore an editor group in a multi-group editor grid
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command calls EditorPart.arrangeGroups/toggleMaximizeGroup, GridView.maximizeView/exitMaximizedView traverses grid leaves, and each affected branch synchronously toggles the child `.visible` class and relayouts its SplitView. The changed CSS selector is evaluated by browser style resolution before the next paint; no external operation blocks progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of editor-group leaves and, for selector matching, the number of direct children in each grid branch after nesting. A visibility change can invalidate following siblings, but the selector remains scoped to one SplitView branch and maximization coalesces browser style calculation until rendering; typical branch cardinality is small.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All visibility mutation, SplitView layout, style invalidation, and paint scheduling are serialized on the renderer main thread. There is no task fan-out or concurrent boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. Browser style-rule caching/invalidation applies equally to cold and warm runs; the diff changes the selector predicate but introduces no cache key, retained result, or repeated miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous style path and before/after behavior: the old rule matched every non-first DOM child, while the new rule matches visible children that have a preceding visible sibling. No forced style read was added to production code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser selector-invalidation cost depends on Chromium internals and group topology, but direct-child cardinality is small and the existing maximize path already performs per-view relayout. There is no evidence of a user-visible increase in frame time.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The selector adds a preceding-sibling visibility test, but it removes pseudo-elements from hidden/first-visible views and does not add forced layout, boundary calls, unbounded work, or a realistic high-cardinality hot path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or toggle visibility in other SplitView users with a non-transparent separator, such as merge editor grids and responsive multi-diff panes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SplitView construction or setViewVisible mutates DOM classes and inline geometry; the browser resolves the separator rule during normal style/layout before paint. Responsive callers may toggle visibility during layout, but the diff itself adds no synchronous geometry read and no extra JavaScript iteration.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Direct child views in the individual SplitView. The general-sibling selector scans only preceding siblings within that container; with all views visible, the immediately preceding child satisfies it, and hidden gaps contribute at most their local sibling span.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer-main-thread serialized DOM/style work. Multiple visibility updates can be coalesced by the browser before paint; there is no limiter, queue, IPC, or asynchronous concurrency change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No repository cache, memoization, or negative-cache behavior is touched. Warm browser style data may reduce matching cost, but the performance conclusion does not depend on it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the CSS scope, SplitView.style activation logic, and setViewVisible call path. The added test performs forced getComputedStyle reads only in test code and therefore does not reach product scenarios.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Some SplitView consumers can be updated during window layout, but non-transparent separator users have low direct-child counts. No benchmark is present, yet the changed mechanism does not establish meaningful latency or dropped frames at realistic scale.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Runtime work remains normal style matching on an already-relayouted small collection, while the test-only computed-style reads do not affect shipped performance.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced separator matching through SplitView visibility changes, grid maximization/restoration, and representative non-editor consumers. The only relevant family was synchronous UI work; the change introduces no forced production layout, expensive boundary, concurrency burst, retained state, or realistically scaling performance regression. No findings were submitted.
